title: a16z Podcast: The Future of Food

reader_summary.source_label: From the episode notes — transcript not yet available
reader_summary.headline: Rob Rhinehart, like most startup entrepreneurs, was strapped for cash and time as developed his ideas and ultimately a company.
reader_summary.overview: Rob Rhinehart, like most startup entrepreneurs, was strapped for cash and time as developed his ideas and ultimately a company. What stood out to Rhinehart in that all-consuming and ongoing process was the contrast between all the things in his life that technology had made more convenient and cheaper -- basically everything powered by smartphones -- and what he felt was a process still trapped in our agrarian past.

key_points.text: Out of that observation came Soylent -- nutrition in powder or ready-to-drink form.
Better, faster, cheaper -- Soylent has all the trademarks of good tech -- but are we really going to start drinking our meals?
Rhinehart joins this segment of the pod along with a16z’s Chris Dixon, who led the firm’s investment in Soylent.
